headline: Brigatinib in ROS1-positive NSCLC: median overall survival 43.9 months in TKI-naive patients
dek: Updated Barossa study data show median overall survival of 43.9 months in TKI-naive patients and 12.2 months after crizotinib, according to oncologist Stephen V Liu.
body:
Updated survival results from the Barossa study of brigatinib in ROS1-positive tumours have been reported, according to a post on X by Stephen V Liu, MD, which tagged the JTO journal account.

In 47 patients with TKI-naive ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), Liu wrote, median overall survival was 43.9 months. Overall survival was 50% at three years and 36% at five years.

For patients treated after crizotinib, median overall survival was 12.2 months, with overall survival of 37% at three years and 11% at five years.

Liu also wrote that 71% to 74% of patients went on to receive subsequent therapies.
key_quote: In 47 pts with TKI naive ROS1+ NSCLC, mOS 43.9m, 3y OS 50%, 5y OS 36%.
